settings.heading: Same room. Same bulb wattage. Different light.
settings.subheading: CRI is the spec most lighting brands hope you never ask about.

settings.heading: A scale to 100. Most LEDs stop at 80.
settings.text1: CRI — Colour Rendering Index — measures how faithfully a light source shows colour compared with natural light, on a scale to 100. Sunlight scores 100. A candle scores close to 100. Most LED lighting sold in Singapore scores around 80.
settings.text2: At Ra80, roughly a fifth of colour fidelity is gone — and it is not lost evenly. Reds fade first. Wood turns grey-brown, leather goes flat, skin looks tired, food looks less fresh. The room is bright, but everything in it is slightly wrong.
settings.highlight: Nothing in the room changed. Only the light did.

settings.heading: See it on the same room.
settings.caption: Illustration of the effect. Colour rendering varies by object and light source.

settings.heading: R9: the one nobody publishes.
settings.text1: Here is the part most brands leave out. The general CRI score (Ra) averages only eight pastel test colours — none of them a saturated red. Red rendering is measured separately, as R9. A bulb can score Ra80 while its R9 sits near zero.
settings.text2: Red matters more than any other colour at home. It is in skin tones, timber, leather, brick, tomatoes, a glass of wine. Low R9 is why food photographs badly in some kitchens and why faces look washed out in some mirrors.
settings.card1: Every KAYVA product is Ra95+ with R9 above 50, and both numbers are backed by an independent test report. If we cannot verify a spec, we do not print it.
settings.card2: Ra95+ is the standard museums and galleries specify. Your home holds the things you chose — it deserves the same standard.

settings.heading: High CRI costs lumens.
settings.text: A Ra95+ bulb produces less raw brightness than a Ra80 bulb of the same wattage, because rendering colour faithfully takes energy that would otherwise go to raw output. We think the trade is worth making — you renovated for colour and texture, not for lux readings. But you should know it exists.

settings.title: Ask for the test report
settings.text: Not the listing claim. The report names the lab, the sample, and the date.

settings.title: Read Ra and R9 separately
settings.text: If a brand publishes only "high CRI" with no number, or a number with no report, treat it as Ra80 until proven otherwise.

settings.title: Then choose colour temperature
settings.text: CRI is half the decision. Our Kelvin guide covers the other half.
